Description - SessionBegin

Not verified live. After a successful Auth, and only if [proto-webox] session-enabled=true (default false), the client posts this SOAP message (SOAPAction http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin, gzip disabled for this message) to http://<session host>/session, where the session host is [proto-webox] webservice-session or session.box. + domain. The client reads nothing from the reply.

Live status: not verifiable. The main service does not implement SessionBegin (a:ActionNotSupported, see soapEndpoint example main-endpoint-not-supported), session.box.chomikuj.pl has no DNS record, and http://box.chomikuj.pl/session redirects to an error page (probeSessionPath). No credentials were sent to any session host. Both examples below are derived from the client's behaviour.

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Server. This path item targets the session host, not the main service.

Path notes

URL http://<session host>/session used only by SessionBegin. The GET operation documents a live probe of the same path on the main host.

Parameters

Parameters of SessionBegin
NameInRequiredTypeDescriptionExample
SOAPActionheaderrequiredstring = "http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin"

WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give a:ActionNotSupported.

http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin
Content-Encodingheaderoptionalstring one of "gzip"

Present when the body is gzip-compressed ([network] soap-use-gzip=true in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (Auth/success vs Auth/success-uncompressed-request). SessionBegin is sent with soap:gzip=false, so the client never sets it here.

Request - body and examples

Body required.

SOAP 1.1 request envelope for SessionBegin (media type text/xml, charset UTF-8).

Body text/xml

Schema

Schema SessionBeginRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SessionBeginRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for SessionBegin: <s:Envelope><s:Body><SessionBegin xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <SessionBegin> object required SessionBeginRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element SessionBegin in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <name> string required

          Account login name.

        • <passHash> string required

          MD5 of the password, as in Auth.

        • <ver> integer (int32) required

          Always 4.

        • <client> object required SessionClientInfo

          Client identification including the OS string.

          • <name> string required

            Always chomikbox.

          • <version> string required

            Always 2.0.8.2.

          • <os> string required

            Operating-system string: OS: %1 (ver. %2.%3) Build(%4) Architecture: %5 Service Pack %6.%7.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check SessionBeginResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema SessionBeginResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SessionBeginResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for SessionBegin: <s:Envelope><s:Body><SessionBeginResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><SessionBeginResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <SessionBeginResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <SessionBeginResult> object required SessionBeginResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string optional nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Not present on the main service (17 of the 18 client operations exist there).

Security notes - findings that concern SessionBegin

  • C-01 High All client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it.
  • C-02 High The login credential passHash is an unsalted MD5 of the password, sent in clear in every Auth: it is password-equivalent and cheap to crack.
  • S-12 Low session.box.chomikuj.pl (SessionBegin) no longer resolves in DNS; whoever registered it would receive the user name and password hash from old clients with session-enabled=true (off by default).

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
